name: Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS)
directions: Clinician-rated from a clinical interview. Rate the stated interval and record it in the assessment notes. Choose one score from 0 to 6 for each item using the authorized item anchors. This is a severity measure, not a diagnosis or safety assessment.

questions.definition: 0 No sadness; 2 looks dispirited but brightens readily; 4 appears sad and unhappy most of the time; 6 miserable and extremely despondent.
0 occasional, circumstance-appropriate sadness; 2 sad or low but brightens readily; 4 pervasive sadness still influenced by circumstances; 6 continuous misery or despondency.
0 placid, fleeting tension; 2 occasional edginess; 4 continuous tension or intermittent panic with difficulty mastering it; 6 overwhelming dread or anguish.
0 usual sleep; 2 slight difficulty or slightly reduced/fitful sleep; 4 sleep reduced or broken by at least two hours; 6 less than two or three hours.
0 normal or increased; 2 slightly reduced; 4 no appetite or food tasteless; 6 needs persuasion to eat.
0 none; 2 occasional difficulty collecting thoughts; 4 difficulty sustaining thought that limits reading or conversation; 6 unable to read or converse without great difficulty.
0 hardly any difficulty starting; 2 difficulty starting activities; 4 simple routine activities require effort; 6 unable to do anything without help.
0 normal interest and emotional response; 2 reduced ability to enjoy usual interests; 4 loss of interest/feelings; 6 emotionally paralysed or painful failure to feel for close others.
0 none; 2 fluctuating failure/self-reproach ideas; 4 persistent self-accusation or rational guilt and increasing pessimism; 6 delusions of ruin/remorse or absurd, unshakable self-accusation.
0 enjoys life; 2 weary of life or fleeting suicidal thoughts; 4 suicidal thoughts common and considered as a solution without specific plans/intention; 6 explicit plans and active preparation.

attribution: Montgomery SA, Åsberg M. A new depression scale designed to be sensitive to change. Br J Psychiatry. 1979;134:382–389.
